style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: Four verses, and the whole posture of prayer in a picture: as the eyes of a servant are on the master's hand, and the eyes of a maidservant on her mistress's hand, so our eyes are on the LORD our God until He is gracious. The pilgrim on the road up to Jerusalem lifts his eyes past the hills to the One enthroned in the heavens, and then he explains what the lifted eyes mean -- not admiration but attention, the servant's watch for the hand that signals, gives, or corrects. The second half is the reason for the watching: we have had more than our fill of contempt; our soul is stuffed with the mockery of the complacent and the contempt of the arrogant -- the returned exiles, perhaps, among neighbors who laughed at their wall (Nehemiah 2:19; 4:1-3). No answer comes inside the psalm. The prayer is simply to keep looking, and it is enough.

1.text: A song of ascents. To You I lift up my eyes -- You who sit enthroned in the heavens.
1.amp: A Song [shir] of degrees [maaloth]. Unto You lift I up [nasa] mine eyes [ayin], O You that dwell [yashab -- sit enthroned] in the heavens [shamayim].
1.notes: elekha nasati et-enai (H5375, H5869): the eyes lifted -- Psalm 121's 'I lift up my eyes to the hills' carried past the hills to their Maker: ha-yoshevi ba-shamayim (H3427, H8064), to the One who SITS in the heavens, enthroned. The pilgrim's eyes go past the hills to the throne.

2.text: Look -- as the eyes of servants are on the hand of their master, as the eyes of a maidservant are on the hand of her mistress, so our eyes are on the LORD our God, until He shows us grace.
2.amp: Behold, as the eyes [ayin] of servants [ebed] look unto the hand [yad] of their masters [adon], and as the eyes of a maiden [shiphchah -- maidservant] unto the hand of her mistress [gebereth]; so our eyes wait upon the LORD [YHWH] our God [Elohim], until that He have mercy [chanan -- be gracious] upon us.
2.notes: ke-ene avadim el-yad adonehem (H5869, H5650, H3027, H113), ke-ene shiphchah el-yad gebirtah (H8198, H1404): as the eyes of servants to their master's hand, of a maidservant to her mistress's hand -- watching the HAND for the signal, the gift, the correction -- ken enenu el-YHWH Elohenu (H3068, H430): so our eyes are on the LORD our God, ad she-yechonnenu (H2603): until He is gracious. Patience pictured as a household's attentiveness; the eyes do not leave the hand.

3.text: Be gracious to us, O LORD, be gracious to us, for we have had more than our fill of contempt.
3.amp: Have mercy [chanan -- be gracious] upon us, O LORD [YHWH], have mercy upon us: for we are exceedingly [rav] filled [saba -- sated] with contempt [buz].
3.notes: chonnenu YHWH chonnenu (H2603): grace asked twice, as in Psalm 57:1 -- ki-rav savanu buz (H7227, H7646, H937): we are MORE than sated with buz, contempt -- saba is the word for a full stomach; they have eaten scorn until they are sick of it. A setting like the returned exiles' among their sneering neighbors fits the psalm well (cf. Nehemiah 2:19, where the same roots describe Sanballat's mockery), though the psalm itself is undated.

4.text: Our soul has had more than its fill of the mockery of the complacent, of the contempt of the arrogant.
4.amp: Our soul [nephesh] is exceedingly [rav] filled [saba] with the scorning [laag -- mockery] of those that are at ease [shaanan -- complacent, secure], and with the contempt [buz] of the proud [gayon -- the arrogant; qere geah yonim, the proud oppressors].
4.notes: rabbat saveah-lah naphshenu (H7227, H7646, H5315): the soul stuffed with ha-laag ha-shaanannim (H3933, H7600) -- the mockery of the comfortable, those at ease -- ha-buz li-geeyonim (H937, H1349): the contempt of the arrogant. The psalm ends without an answer; the eyes are still on the hand. That is the whole prayer: to keep looking.
